title: Modifying and Searching Array Elements
learningObjectives: Explain modifying and searching array elements.
Describe relevant storage, indexing and size rules.
Trace a collection operation or traversal.
Recognize bounds, lifetime or input pitfalls.
Apply the type to a practical collection task.

understand.concept: Element assignment updates a selected value. Search scans for a target and may record a match or position; initialize search state.
understand.whyItMatters: Searching and updating are core collection tasks.
understand.explain: Define first/last match behavior, guard indexes and initialize result variables.

examples.title: Search flag
examples.explanation: Stop at the target and set the flag.

examples.title: Find index
examples.explanation: Position 1 is recorded; -1 means no match.

examples.title: Replace negative values
examples.explanation: Reference iteration modifies the original elements.

practise.guidedTask: Trace all five Modifying and Searching Array Elements examples. Record sizes, indexes, values and condition checks. Identify first/last valid element and relevant edge cases.
practise.independentTask: Create a small C++ data-processing program demonstrating modifying and searching array elements. Test typical values, empty/boundary cases, and invalid input or indexing where relevant. Explain why this collection is appropriate.
hints: Use zero-based indexes and verify bounds.
Prefer range-based traversal when index is unnecessary.
Check emptiness before operations such as front or pop_back.
Test first, last and invalid boundaries.
